description: Schema for Gartner Buyer Voice analysis using GEAR end-user interaction exports, formatted corpus files, prompt-guided discovery, qualitative theme ratings, traceable evidence, and validation checks.
intent: Model Gartner buyer interaction corpora as traceable evidence for Buyer Voice analysis. The schema preserves raw GEAR records, normalizes buyer and analyst context, supports unconstrained theme discovery and supplied-category organization, applies qualitative ratings, and validates every deliverable claim against source references, excerpts, attribution, and redaction rules.
scope: This schema applies to buyer voice projects built from Gartner end-user interaction records. It supports discovered-theme analysis, market-cut analysis, and client-supplied category analysis while preserving raw interaction provenance and evidence attribution.

metadata.score_subject: Buyer Voice vendor corpus/report package readiness

scoring_logic.0: No usable evidence or schema support is present.
scoring_logic.1: Raw source material exists but is not organized into a reproducible Buyer Voice workflow.
scoring_logic.2: Core source data is present and partially normalized, but traceability, ratings, or report packaging are incomplete.
scoring_logic.3: Dataset is structured enough for standard report production with clear corpus definition, themes, ratings, and evidence expectations.
scoring_logic.4: Dataset is report-ready with strong provenance, explicit analysis scope, evidence linkage, validation checks, and deliverable guardrails.
scoring_logic.5: Dataset is fully productionized with automated ingestion, evidence ledger validation, redaction checks, and closed-loop report QA.

canonical_inputs: Corpora - Raw GEAR/GEAR - ServiceNow Commercial Friction Set.csv

principles.label: Raw Export Preservation
principles.statement: The raw GEAR CSV export is the canonical data source. Derived formatted text files are useful for model ingestion but must not replace the raw record.

principles.label: Unconstrained Discovery First
principles.statement: Themes are discovered from the corpus before any category list, market definition, or vendor taxonomy is used to organize them.

principles.label: Evidence Is First Class
principles.statement: Every theme rating and substantive buyer-voice claim must resolve to source interaction records, reference numbers, and verbatim excerpts.

principles.label: Buyer Voice Attribution
principles.statement: Question Asked is direct buyer framing. Discussion Summary must be used, but statements from it require buyer, analyst, or uncertain attribution.

principles.label: Qualitative Ratings
principles.statement: Spread and trajectory are qualitative judgments. Counts may inform the judgment but are not emitted as slide-facing output unless explicitly authorized.

principles.label: Validation Before Publication
principles.statement: Claims, ratings, references, buyer composition, and redaction must be checked before output reaches a deliverable.

SRC.name: Source Corpus
SRC.focus: Define, preserve, and reproduce the Buyer Voice source package: raw GEAR exports, formatted text corpora, prompts, rubric, scripts, and slide examples.
evidence_signals: raw CSV artifact registered as canonical source
formatted corpus files linked as derived artifacts
prompt, rubric, and deck references preserved
row counts and date windows recorded

INT.name: Interaction Record
INT.focus: Normalize each GEAR interaction into durable buyer, analyst, vendor, date, lifecycle, and text fields while retaining all raw columns.
evidence_signals: Reference Number resolves to a raw row
Question Asked and Discussion Summary preserved
buyer region, industry, role, persona, and market retained

RUN.name: Analysis Run and Scope
RUN.focus: Represent each analytical pass, its prompts, scoping mode, qualifying record set, market cuts, supplied categories, and comparison windows.

THM.name: Theme Discovery
THM.focus: Capture buyer-language themes discovered from the corpus before organizing them into market cuts or supplied categories.

RAT.name: Qualitative Rating
RAT.focus: Apply fixed qualitative rating criteria after discovery: Spread, Trajectory, Persistent, optional sentiment, and competitive scenarios.
evidence_signals: counts kept out of slide-facing output

EVD.name: Evidence and Voice
EVD.focus: Keep every claim traceable to reference numbers, source fields, verbatim excerpts, and buyer-versus-analyst voice attribution.
evidence_signals: client-identifying details redacted before deliverable use

OUT.name: Deliverable Claims
OUT.focus: Model slide/report claims separately from source evidence, including manual titles, kicker lines, synthesis panels, handling notes, and buyer quotes.

VAL.name: Validation and Governance
VAL.focus: Check that references, claims, role/region/industry composition, figures, attribution, ratings, and redaction are supported before publication.

SRC-01.name: Source Package Inventory
SRC-01.definition: Register every file in the Buyer Voice package and classify it as canonical source, derived source, method reference, or deliverable reference.

SRC-02.name: Corpus Definition
SRC-02.definition: Define each analysis corpus, including anchor logic, raw files, formatted files, record count, date range, and known limitations.

SRC-03.name: Formatted Corpus Reproducibility
SRC-03.definition: Track the NotebookLM-oriented text outputs as reproducible projections of raw GEAR data, not as canonical data.

INT-01.name: Canonical Interaction Spine
INT-01.definition: Preserve the Reference Number, dates, subtype, purpose, question, summary, lifecycle fields, and raw GEAR fields for each interaction.

INT-02.name: Buyer Profile
INT-02.definition: Normalize buyer-side metadata used to support role, region, industry, sector, market, persona, and enterprise-size claims.

INT-03.name: Analyst and Vendor Context
INT-03.definition: Retain Gartner associate metadata and vendor/product context without over-attributing ambiguous product mentions.

RUN-01.name: Run Provenance
RUN-01.definition: Capture the analytical pass, source corpus, prompt references, rubric version, run status, and deliverable artifacts.

RUN-02.name: Explicit Qualifying Set
RUN-02.definition: Make the exact record set used for a scope or rating explicit so Spread and trajectory are assessed against the right base.

RUN-03.name: Scoping Mode
RUN-03.definition: Differentiate discovered, market-cut, and supplied-category workflows while preserving unconstrained discovery first.

THM-01.name: Buyer-Language Theme
THM-01.definition: Represent discovered themes in buyer language and preserve theme history across merges, renames, and period comparisons.

THM-02.name: Supplied Category Assignment
THM-02.definition: Attach themes to supplied categories only after discovery, retaining themes that do not fit as appendix or out-of-scope findings.

RAT-01.name: Spread Rating
RAT-01.definition: Rate how consistently and broadly a theme recurs across the qualifying set using Pervasive, Significant, Moderate, or Niche.
validation_rules: No numeric thresholds in v1.0
Assess against qualifying records
Do not emit counts in slide output

RAT-02.name: Trajectory and Persistence
RAT-02.definition: Compare two windows using New, Intensifying, Stable, or Fading, with Persistent captured as a separate boolean.
validation_rules: Require at least ten supporting records per comparison window
Require Spread of at least Moderate
Use insufficient-volume note when gate fails

RAT-03.name: Optional Sentiment and Scenario
RAT-03.definition: Capture sentiment and competitive situations only when the analysis has a named target or data-derived commercial scenario.
validation_rules: Do not force sentiment onto broad market/problem themes
Do not introduce a fixed competitive scenario taxonomy

EVD-01.name: Source Field Attribution
EVD-01.definition: Identify whether evidence comes from Question Asked, Discussion Summary, Both, Purpose, or another field.

EVD-02.name: Voice Attribution
EVD-02.definition: Classify evidence as buyer voice, buyer-raised in summary, analyst voice, or attribution uncertain before using it in a finding.

EVD-03.name: Redaction Status
EVD-03.definition: Track whether excerpts contain client-identifying detail and whether they are safe for deliverable use.

OUT-01.name: Deliverable Claim
OUT-01.definition: Represent slide/report statements separately from evidence so manual authoring and support status remain visible.

OUT-02.name: Output Policy
OUT-02.definition: Distinguish slide-facing output from audit output, especially around counts, reference numbers, excerpts, and internal-only notes.
validation_rules: No counts in slide output by default
No reference numbers on slides by default
Audit output may include counts and references

VAL-01.name: Reference and Evidence Checks
VAL-01.definition: Ensure every cited reference resolves and every rating has supporting evidence.
validation_rules: Unresolved references are blockers
Ratings without references are blockers
Single-record claims cannot be presented as themes

VAL-02.name: Claim Support Checks
VAL-02.definition: Verify that role, region, industry, figure, trajectory, and composition claims are supported by cited records.
validation_rules: Unsupported figures are errors
Unsupported buyer composition claims are errors
Middle-clustered ratings require review

VAL-03.name: Voice and Redaction Checks
VAL-03.definition: Block analyst-voice leakage into buyer findings and client-identifying detail in deliverable output.
validation_rules: Analyst voice is never buyer voice
Attribution-uncertain statements must be labeled
Redaction-required findings are blockers

source_package.description: A bundled project input package containing source exports, formatted corpora, prompts, rubric, and example deliverables.

source_artifact.description: One file in the source package.

corpus.description: A coherent set of interaction records used as the input universe for one or more analyses.

interaction.description: One Gartner end-user interaction record from a GEAR CSV export.
normalization_rules: Treat '-' and blank strings as null for normalized fields.
Derive quarter from first_response_date as 'YYYY QN'.
Split Personal Tags into an array on commas, trimming whitespace.
Do not drop records solely because vendor_name is blank or '-'.

buyer_profile.description: Buyer-side metadata associated with an interaction.

analyst_profile.description: Gartner associate metadata associated with an interaction.

vendor_context.description: Vendor and product context present in the GEAR record.
notes: Vendor Name may be '-' even when vendor or product terms appear in question_asked or discussion_summary.
For OpenAI corpora, bare 'GPT' should be flagged as ambiguous unless the surrounding context supports OpenAI attribution.
Azure OpenAI should preserve both OpenAI technology relevance and Microsoft commercial relationship.

formatted_corpus_file.description: A NotebookLM-oriented text file generated from a raw corpus.

analysis_run.description: One end-to-end analytical pass or project deliverable built from a corpus and prompts.

analysis_scope.description: The record cut used for an analysis run or theme rating.

supplied_category.description: A top-level category supplied by a client team or requester. Themes may be organized under it after discovery.
rules: Supplied categories must not constrain initial discovery.
Themes discovered outside supplied categories must be retained as out_of_scope_or_appendix themes rather than discarded.

theme.description: A buyer-language pattern discovered from multiple interactions.
rules: Theme names must use buyer language rather than vendor or Gartner terminology.
A theme must rest on multiple distinct interactions from more than one buyer.
A single-record pattern must be marked isolated_observation, not theme.
If a recurring theme is absent in a period, mark it Not Present rather than assigning a low rating.

theme_rating.description: Qualitative assessment of a theme after discovery.

spread_definitions.Pervasive: Surfaces across nearly all conversations in the qualifying set; near-universal across buyer types and segments.
spread_definitions.Significant: Common and recurring across a large share of conversations; a clear pattern but not universal.
spread_definitions.Moderate: Present in a meaningful minority; real and repeated but concentrated in certain buyer types or use cases.
spread_definitions.Niche: Appears in a small number of conversations; specific to particular buyers, sub-segments, or use cases.

trajectory_definitions.New: Absent or negligible in the earlier comparison window and materially present in the recent one.
trajectory_definitions.Stable: Present at comparable levels in both comparison windows.

rules: Spread is assessed against the qualifying records in the cut being analyzed, not the full corpus by default.
No numeric thresholds are defined for Spread in version 1.0.
Counts inform the rating but do not appear in slide-facing output.
Trajectory requires at least ten supporting records in each comparison window and Spread of at least Moderate.
Themes that fail the trajectory volume gate receive null trajectory and an insufficient-volume note.
Persistent is a separate boolean and must not be encoded as a trajectory value.
Every rating must include supporting references and excerpts.

theme_sentiment.description: Optional prose characterization of buyer sentiment when the analysis has a target for sentiment to attach to.
rules: Run only when sentiment attaches to a named vendor, product, or commercial arrangement.
Do not score sentiment on a fixed scale in version 1.0.
Do not run sentiment for broad market or problem analyses without a clear target.

competitive_scenario.description: Optional data-named commercial situation associated with a theme.
rules: Do not impose a fixed taxonomy for competitive scenarios.
Name scenarios from the data for each project.

theme_evidence.description: A source-backed evidence item supporting a theme, rating, or claim.
rules: Reference numbers must be written out in full as plain text.
Every reference_number must resolve to an interaction in the source corpus.
Buyer questions must remain verbatim except for documented layout shortening.
Discussion Summary excerpts must not be presented as buyer voice unless voice_attribution is buyer_raised_in_summary or buyer_voice.
Analyst voice may support a labeled analyst observation but must not be mixed into buyer-voice findings.

analyst_observation.description: A labeled observation from analyst commentary rather than direct buyer voice.
rules: Analyst commentary is not Gartner institutional position.
Use analyst observations only as labeled supporting color, preferably when several distinct analysts observe the same pattern.

deliverable_claim.description: A claim, title, card statement, synthesis line, or output element intended for a slide or report.
rules: Titles, kicker lines, and synthesis panels may be manually authored and have no direct supporting records, but must still be checked against the corpus as authored claims.
No unsupported figure or count should pass validation.
No client-identifying detail should pass to a deliverable.

validation_finding.description: A machine or human validation issue found during claim, evidence, rating, or redaction review.

openai_2026_ytd.name: OpenAI - GGM Power POC July 2026
scoping_examples: Discovered themes across full OpenAI-anchored corpus
Discovered themes within Enterprise AI Assistants market cut
Discovered themes within Enterprise AI Coding Agents market cut

required_validation_checks.label: Reference Resolution
required_validation_checks.description: Every cited reference number must resolve to a raw interaction in the analysis corpus.

required_validation_checks.label: Evidence Presence
required_validation_checks.description: Every theme rating must have at least one supporting evidence item and every theme must rest on multiple distinct buyer interactions unless marked isolated_observation.

required_validation_checks.label: Buyer Voice Attribution
required_validation_checks.description: Evidence from Discussion Summary must be attributed as buyer-raised, analyst voice, or attribution uncertain before being used.

required_validation_checks.label: Analyst Voice Separation
required_validation_checks.description: Gartner recommendations, market statistics, and analyst reads must not be mixed into buyer-voice findings.

required_validation_checks.label: Buyer Composition Support
required_validation_checks.description: Claims about roles, industries, sectors, or regions must be supported by the cited records.

required_validation_checks.label: Figure Provenance
required_validation_checks.description: Any count, percentage, price, or numerical claim must appear in the corpus or be explicitly marked as external/manual.

required_validation_checks.label: Redaction
required_validation_checks.description: Named organizations, prices, seat counts, headcounts, and other client-identifying details must be removed before deliverable use.

required_validation_checks.label: Discovery Integrity
required_validation_checks.description: Supplied categories or market labels must not constrain the initial discovery step.

required_validation_checks.label: Trajectory Volume Gate
required_validation_checks.description: Trajectory may be assigned only when the theme has enough supporting records in both comparison windows and Spread is at least Moderate.

required_validation_checks.label: Rating Distribution Review
required_validation_checks.description: If most themes cluster in the middle values, flag the run for review.

implementation_notes: Start ingestion from raw CSV files, not formatted text files.
Use formatted text files only as reproducibility artifacts for the NotebookLM workflow.
Preserve all raw GEAR columns in interaction.raw_fields even when normalized fields are extracted.
Use analysis_scope.qualifying_reference_numbers as the explicit rating base.
Avoid deriving numeric spread thresholds until enough completed projects exist to calibrate them empirically.
Keep validation artifacts separate from slide-facing output.
